chunks.arabic_text: رِجَالُ الْكَشِّيِّ: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مَسْعُودٍ، عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ فَضَالٍ، عَنِ الْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ عَامِرٍ وَ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ حَكِيمٍ، عَنْ أَبَانَ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ الْأَحْمَرِ، عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ

translations.en: Rijal al-Kashshi: Muhammad ibn Mas'ud, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal, from al-Abbas ibn A'mir and Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Hukaym, from Aban ibn Uthman al-Ahmar, from Abi Basir who said:

chunks.arabic_text: كُنْتُ جَالِسًا عِنْدَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ إِذْ جَاءَتْ أُمُّ خَالِدٍ الَّتِي قَطَعَهَا يُوسُفُ تَسْتَأْذِنُ عَلَيْهِ، قَالَ، فَقَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: أَيُسْرِكَ أَنْ تَشْهَدَ كَلَامَهَا قَالَ: فَقُلْتُ: نَعَمْ جَعَلْتُ فَدَاكَ، فَقَالَ: أَمَا الْآنَ فَأَدْنِ، قَالَ: فَأَجْلَسَنِي عَلَى الطَّنْفَسَةِ، ثُمَّ دَخَلَتْ فَتَكَلَّمَتْ فَإِذَا هِيَ امْرَأَةٌ بَلِيغَةٌ، فَسَأَلَتْهُ عَنْ فُلَانٍ وَ فُلَانٍ، فَقَالَ لَهَا: تَوَلِّيهِمَا قَالَتْ: فَأَقُولُ لِرَبِّي إِذَا لَقِيتُهُ إِنَّكَ أَمَرْتَنِي بِوَلَايَتِهِمَا؟ قَالَ: نَعَمْ قَالَتْ: فَإِنَّ هَذَا الَّذِي مَعَكَ عَلَى الطَّنْفَسَةِ يُأْمِرُنِي بِالْبَرَاءَةِ مِنْهُمَا، وَ كَثِيرُ النَّوَاءِ يُأْمِرُنِي بِوَلَايَتِهِمَا فَأَيُّهُمَا أَحَبُّ إِلَيْكَ؟ قَالَ: هَذَا وَ اللَّهِ وَ أَصْحَابُهُ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ مِنْ كَثِيرِ النَّوَاءِ وَ أَصْحَابِهِ، إِنَّ هَذَا يَخَاصِمُ فَيَقُولُ مَنْ لَمْ يَحْكُمْ بِمَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْكَافِرُونَ، وَ مَنْ لَمْ يَحْكُمْ بِمَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الظَّالِمُونَ، وَ مَنْ لَمْ يَحْكُمْ بِمَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْفَاسِقُونَ، فَلَمَّا خَرَجَتْ قَالَ: إِنِّي خَشِيتُ أَنْ تَذْهَبَ فَتُخْبِرَ كَثِيرًا فَيُشْهِرَنِي بِالْكُوفَةِ، اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي إِلَيْكَ مِنْ كَثِيرٍ بَرِيءٌ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَ الْآخِرَةِ

translations.en: I was seated at Abu Abdillah's (peace be upon him) place when Umm Khalid – whose hand had been cut by Yusuf – came seeking permission to see him. He said [to me]: Would you like to hear her speech? I said: Yes, may I be made your ransom. He said: Then draw near, and he made me sit upon the rug. She entered and spoke and I found her to be a very eloquent woman. She asked him about so and so, so he said to her: Deem them to be your leaders. She said: Do you allow me to say to my Lord when I meet him that you ordered me to take them as my authorities? He said: Yes. She said: [I ask this] because this one who is with you on the rug orders me to disassociate from them while Kathir al-Nawwa orders me to take them as authorities, so which one is more beloved to you? He said: This one and his companions are by Allah more beloved to me than Kathir al-Nawwa and his fellows. This one argues by saying: 'Whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed – then it is those who are the disbelievers', 'and whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed – then it is those who are the wrongdoers', 'and whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed – then it is those who are the defiantly disobedient'. So when she had departed he said: I feared that she will go and inform Kathir who would then make this infamous about me in Kufa. O Allah I resort to you in disassociating myself from Kathir in this world and the hereafter.

en.summary: This hadith from Al-Kashi’s *Rijal* highlights the nuanced Shia doctrine of *al-Wala’ wa al-Bara’* (loyalty and disassociation) through a dialogue with Umm Khalid, a prominent companion known for her eloquence. The Imam (peace be upon him) contrasts the steadfastness of Abu Basir, who affirms leadership based on divine decree, with Kathir al-Nawwa, who employs the same Quranic verses to justify political disassociation, thereby illustrating the theological basis for distinguishing between the righteous and the dissenters. The Imam’s subsequent fear of Kathir’s influence in Kufa underscores the practical political implications of this theological stance in early Shia community dynamics.
en.seo_question: Why did the Imam prefer Abu Basir over Kathir al-Nawwa in the presence of Umm Khalid?

key_terms.الْكُوفَةِ: Kufa, a major city in Iraq
